result.search_summary: The core cutting-stock constraints are clear, but the pattern-frequency cost structure and whether all demand must be met exactly remain unresolved.

gaps.description: The extra cost is described by usage-frequency rank, but it is unclear whether the rank is over all used patterns or only over patterns with positive usage, and how ties in frequency are handled.
gaps.direct_question: For the extra pattern cost, should patterns be ranked only among patterns actually used, and if two patterns have the same usage frequency, how should their ranks and costs be assigned?
gaps.why_material: Ranking and tie rules change the objective coefficients and can alter which cutting patterns are selected.

gaps.description: It is not confirmed whether the customer order quantities must be met exactly or whether overproduction is allowed.
gaps.direct_question: Must the cutting plan produce exactly the ordered quantities of each pipe length, or is producing extra pieces acceptable?
gaps.why_material: Exact versus minimum demand changes the feasible set and may change the optimal pattern mix.

gaps.description: The leftover rule says leftover length must not exceed 100 mm for any cutting pattern, but it is unclear whether this is a hard feasibility rule or a soft preference.
gaps.direct_question: Is the 100 mm maximum leftover per cutting pattern a strict requirement that every used pattern must satisfy, or is it a preference that can be violated with penalty?
gaps.why_material: Treating leftover as hard versus soft changes which patterns are feasible and whether penalties enter the objective.

gaps.description: The request limits the plan to at most four different cutting patterns, but it is unclear whether unused patterns count toward this limit.
gaps.direct_question: Does the limit of at most four different cutting patterns apply only to patterns actually used, or does it include any pattern considered in the plan?
gaps.why_material: The interpretation changes the combinatorial restriction on the pattern set and can affect feasibility and optimality.
